messages:
carmen: Quick sync - support flagged that dashboards show rollup p50/p95 that conflict with endpoint numbers, causing customers to think performance improved during a rollout. Can we standardize drilldown behavior?

li: Seen it too. Rollups are great for overview but they can use different quantile methods and sample sources. When you drill into a route the UX should prefer the most exact data available.

matt: Agreed. We should add an in-tile mini-compare: small two-line sparkline showing rollup vs endpoint (if endpoint exists) with a tiny toggle "Prefer endpoint". Users can swap in-place.

tess: UX note: prefer-endpoint as a toggle is fine, but product wants a default for SLO dashboards: prefer endpoint automatically and show a small badge explaining why. Non-SLO overview pages keep rollup default.

jamal: Backend constraints: endpoint exacts are only available when raw samples are streamed to central store (hosted clusters). Dedicated/private customers might not have endpoint data centrally, so the prefer-endpoint default should be conditional. We can emit rollup.meta.endpoint_available boolean.

ashley-product: Product supports conditional default. We also want the console API to allow `?prefer=endpoint` so programmatic dashboards can opt in. That helps customers embedding charts in docs.

carmen: Good call. Also add a small provenance pill: external/internal/canary counts so users know why rollup differs.

jamal: Telemetry impact: provenance_counts is a small map (3 fields) per rollup point. Cheap to store. Adding endpoint_available flag and quantile_method/method_confidence should be easy.

matt: For the in-tile compare, front-end can lazy-fetch endpoint series on hover to avoid bandwidth. Minimal UX: two-line legend with tiny dots and the toggle.

li: One more complication: sampling rates differ by route due to quotas and routing policies (we downsample low-traffic tenants for cost). Rollups may merge sampled shards with different rates causing percentile drift. We should include sample_rate metadata per shard or a normalized sample_rate estimate.

jamal: True. We can compute an effective_sample_rate in aggregator (approx) and emit rollup.meta.effective_sample_rate. Helps users see when rollup is heavily sampled and less reliable.

ashley-product: Product wants copy for the badge: "Showing endpoint exacts (preferred for SLOs)" and for rollup: "Rollup (approx) - includes internal/canary traffic". Keep copy short.

oncall-jen: Operational note: changing defaults can affect ad-hoc alerts. We must update alerting docs and ensure SLO evaluation still uses endpoint exacts (it does now). Add a runbook entry: when alerted on latency, check rollup.meta.quantile_method, sample_count, provenance_counts, and endpoint_available.

carmen: Here's a proposed server API snippet for the console to request preferred view:
```http
GET /api/v1/metrics/latency?route=/v1/generate&start=2026-05-01T00:00Z&end=2026-05-01T01:00Z&prefer=endpoint
```
Server will return rollup series and, if prefer=endpoint and endpoint_available, the response will include "primary_series": "endpoint" and a secondary_series: "rollup" array for compare.

li: Nice. For backwards compatibility default prefer parameter to "rollup". Feature-flag the default on SLO pages to "endpoint" where endpoint_available==true.

matt: Dev plan: front-end changes + small backend flags. UX prototype ready; will wire to feature flag. We can ship the badge + toggle behind a flag first week, then flip default on SLO pages after canary.

jamal: Infra tasks: 1) emit rollup.meta.{quantile_method,sample_count,provenance_counts,endpoint_available,effective_sample_rate,confidence} 2) add prefer param handling in metrics API 3) audit job nightly for p50/p95 divergence > 10% on SLO routes. I'll open PRs.

oncall-jen: I'll monitor canary and add an alert when endpoint vs rollup delta spikes for >3 consecutive windows. Also ensure oncall runbook has quick SQL to diagnose:
```sql
SELECT hour, rollup.p50 AS rollup_p50, endpoint.p50 AS endpoint_p50, rollup.meta.sample_count, rollup.meta.effective_sample_rate
FROM latency_rollups rollup
LEFT JOIN latency_endpoints endpoint USING(route,hour)
WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND hour BETWEEN '2026-05-01T00:00' AND '2026-05-01T03:00';
```

deploy-bot: :warning: planned deploy 2026-05-06T10:00Z add-rollup-meta-and-prefer-endpoint (id: aggr-5155)

ashley-product: Timeline: product will ship copy + small docs update. Support will get >FAQ about why numbers differ and how to use the new toggle.

carmen: Thanks. Let's keep the initial rollout behind flag, monitor customer-facing confusion metrics, then flip defaults for SLO dashboards after one week if stable.

-- end of thread --
